page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an Arm-based server instance powered by the Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The instance is configured with 64 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, which is directly bundled with the instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top tier and large-block read bandwidth reaching 314.24 GB/sec. Single-threaded and multi-threaded decompression tasks, such as bzip3, show strong performance, with multi-threaded decompression reaching 221.45 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the strong tier, achieving 43.54 GB/sec in web serving. Standard compute benchmarks, including stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, fall within the average range.

The c4a-standard-16-lssd offers a balanced resource density for Arm-native workloads, combining dedicated physical cores with high-speed local NVMe storage. The lack of simultaneous multithreading means each of the 16 vCPUs corresponds to a full physical core, which provides predictable execution times but limits the thread density compared to x86 hyperthreaded alternatives. The inclusion of local NVMe SSDs provides high-speed local scratch space without requiring network-attached storage overhead, enhancing qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-heavy tasks.

This server configuration is suited for database operations, static web serving, and data processing pipelines that benefit from high memory bandwidth and local NVMe storage. It is also applicable for Arm64 software compilation, containerized microservices, and lightweight LLM text generation tasks.
